pr_title: Extensions.Logging: JsonConsoleFormatter serializes scope and state properties using native json type
pr_body:
This PR changes the `JsonConsoleFormatter` to convert the values of the k/v in state and scope to json native types when it is a built-in value type.

I haven't found a way to remove converters easily from the JsonSerializer.
I used the JsonSerializer as I didn't want to reimplement the logic.

Should I reimplement the serialization logic to avoid the cost of the JsonSerializer? Is there already something available I can reuse?
Should I add support for NullableTypes?

Fixes #39870

/cc @maryamariyan

issue_context.title: JsonConsoleFormatter: number and boolean properties should not be converted to string
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description

Currently the new JsonConsoleFormatter converts all the values of the key/value pairs in both the state and scopes to string.
As json supports numbers and booleans, I think the _built-in value types_ should not be converted to `string`.
Using number would allow to write range queries once ingested on a log analysis system.

/cc @maryamariyan 

#### Sample code
```csharp
logger.LogInformation("This is a message with a {Number}", 1);
```
#### Current result
```json
{
  "Timestamp": "2020-07-23T21:47:33.7369359\u002B01:00",
  "EventId": 0,
  "LogLevel": "Information",
  "Category": "JsonLogging.Program",
  "Message": "This is a message with a 1",
  "Number": "1",
  "{OriginalFormat}": "This is a message with a {Number}",
}
```
#### Expected result

```json
{
  "Timestamp": "2020-07-23T21:47:33.7369359\u002B01:00",
  "EventId": 0,
  "LogLevel": "Information",
  "Category": "JsonLogging.Program",
  "Message": "This is a message with a 1",
  "Number": 1,
  "{OriginalFormat}": "This is a message with a {Number}",
}
```

### Regression?

No, part of a new feature

review_comments:
> I haven't found a way to remove converters easily from the JsonSerializer.
I used the JsonSerializer as I didn't want to reimplement the logic.

> Should I reimplement the serialization logic to avoid the cost of the JsonSerializer? Is there already something available I can reuse?
Should I add support for NullableTypes?

@layomia what are your thoughts on this?

There should be a null-check for null values; [Utf8JsonWriter.WriteNull](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.text.json.utf8jsonwriter.writenull?view=netcore-3.1) should be used in those cases.

[Utf8JsonWriter.WriteNumber](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.text.json.utf8jsonwriter.writenumber?view=netcore-3.1) and [Utf8JsonWriter.WriteBoolean](https://docs.microsoft.comdotnet/api/system.text.json.utf8jsonwriter.writeboolean?view=netcore-3.1) should be used instead of the serializer below.

Using the `WriteX` vs `WritePropertyName` + `WriteXValue` allows for one less method call.

Updated as per feedback.
I have not handled the null case explicitly as I don't think it would ever happen, as the Logger set the value to "(null)".
Worst case scenario it will fall back to the string case which handles null.
Is there a test that captures when `item.Value` is `null`? Just to prevent a regression in the future.

I'm not convinced this is the right place for the test, as a formatter should never get a null value.
We don't have tests at that level so it would require a bit of work to add one but I can do it.
What do you think?
Would a `Debug.Assert(item.Value != null)` be enough instead?

The logic is here https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0f7370baa68c5809f93095cbce9bf614f44cc731/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions/src/LogValuesFormatter.cs#L177-L180

It doesn't look like there is a test, however I think it should be left in a separate PR.
Should I log an issue?

Ah! Good one! Thank you!
I always forget that the `Log` method is public.
I've added the test and changed the behaviour to serialize as null, instead of empty string, given `null` is a possible value when you don't rely on the extension methods.
